AC-2: The screen-state vocabulary matches the mockup's own words and severity rule exactly, with a citation to the mockup source.
AC-3: The navigation section shows RBAC visible-but-refused rendering consistent with C3 and the mockup's console-only pattern.
AC-4: If the alarm lifecycle contract is genuinely new, it stays schema-level and cites C1/C2 for table/job boundaries rather than designing a new execution engine.
AC-5: SNMP status exposure is explicitly distinguished from SNMP-trap-out and from device polling.
AC-6: The feature-contribution contract states concretely how a CAP-RELEASED capability's screen/job-type/alarm-source registration works, referencing C4 and C2 by name.

All six C1-C4,C6,C7 platform/backup contracts (plus C5's amendments) are now MERGED as DRAFT -- FOR PO FREEZE; this movement's job is to CATALOGUE where each of the six baseline directory concerns is already answered by one of them (do not re-answer), and write only the genuinely unowned remainder. docs/design/UI2_0_BASELINE_CONTRACT.md's VISUAL-DESIGN-LANGUAGE row (Material Design 3, decided 2026-09-09) and the mockup analysis it references (a 'neXus 2026 Design Refresh' design canvas: Overview, Devices->Inventory, Configuration->Alignment, Compliance, Operations, Administration, Navigation & components screens) are the UX ground truth for the shared screen-state vocabulary and navigation structure -- the mockup's own classification vocabulary (Aligned/healthy, Member-specific, Local override, Difference observed, Effective drift, Not applicable, Not configured, Stale/provenance) and its RBAC visible-but-refused pattern are exactly what UX-D1..D5 need to formalize; adopt that vocabulary rather than inventing a new one, since baseline section 1 (VISUAL-DESIGN-LANGUAGE) already decided the mockup's UI expressions are 'adopted into the baseline directory (B0-8), not re-decided'. docs/design/NAVIGATION_INFORMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md (FROZEN, Line-1's own left-rail navigation contract, fifteen frozen D-NAV decisions) is the closest existing owner for navigation structure -- check whether UI 2.0's navigation should reference its PRINCIPLES (one-root-per-domain, availability-rule-gated visibility) while being its own document (since UI 2.0 is a separate shell per CON.0-AMENDMENT), or whether it needs no new text at all beyond a citation.

The shared screen-state vocabulary is adopted from the M3 mockup's own words (Aligned/healthy, Member-specific, Local override [intentional], Difference observed [unclassified], Effective drift [fault], Not applicable, Not configured, Stale/provenance) and from the mockup's own stated rule ('red is reserved for real fault, unsafe drift, out-of-sync and failure; expected member differences carry no warning icon and no failure wording') -- do not invent a competing vocabulary

RBAC visible-but-refused (C3 section 5/6) is the navigation model's enforcement mechanism -- the navigation section must show how a nav entry the actor's role cannot use is rendered visible-with-reason, not hidden, consistent with both C3 and the mockup's own 'Collect now... console only' pattern

The alarm lifecycle contract (outbox, de-duplication, resolve/silence, delivery failure, causality limits) is new text if no existing document owns it -- check first (search for an existing ALERT/ALARM design doc); if genuinely new, keep it schema-level (referencing C1's table-ownership model and C2's job/notification boundary), not a full implementation design

SNMP status exposure (the product answering NMS reads about its own/its devices' recorded state) is explicitly NOT device polling -- restate this distinction from workflow section 5 B2-5b clearly so it is never confused with the SNMP-trap-out capability

entries.text:
DELIVERED: docs/design/UI2_0_BASELINE_DIRECTORY.md (DRAFT -- FOR PRODUCT OWNER FREEZE). PR #172 MERGED (merge commit 23df8f9d174f1837e11d2a50f67ecb771a044a57). Self-check against AC-1..AC-8:
AC-1 (each of the six concerns has an explicit owner statement): SATISFIED -- section 2 cites NAVIGATION_INFORMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md (FROZEN) + C3 sections 5/6; section 3 cites the mockup + VISUAL-DESIGN-LANGUAGE; section 4 states 'no existing document owns this end to end' and supplies new minimal text tying C4+C2; section 5 states 'genuinely new -- no existing document owns it' with the search performed named explicitly; section 6 cites C1 section 4 directly, no new text; section 7 cites workflow section 5 B2-5b and restates its distinction.
AC-2 (screen-state vocabulary matches the mockup's own words and severity rule exactly, with citation): SATISFIED -- section 3.1/3.2 reproduce the eight-term vocabulary and the exact severity sentence verbatim from this movement's own session packet (the 'neXus 2026 Design Refresh' design canvas), cited as the source; section 3.3 adds an explicitly informative (non-binding) alignment table against Line-1's own frozen states, not a substitute vocabulary.
AC-3 (navigation shows RBAC visible-but-refused rendering consistent with C3 and the mockup's console-only pattern): SATISFIED -- section 2.2 ties C3 section 5.2/5.4's action_affordance/reason_code rendering directly to the mockup's 'Collect now... console only' example named in the task packet.
AC-4 (alarm lifecycle, if genuinely new, stays schema-level and cites C1/C2 for table/job boundaries): SATISFIED -- section 5 confirms no existing owner (FAILOVER_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md and C6 checked and named), then stays at table/state-machine sketch level throughout (5.3-5.5), citing C1's audit-trigger/data-class pattern and C2's job-state-machine/idempotency/OUTCOME_UNKNOWN pattern by section number throughout; explicitly defers rule authoring, channel schemas and retry/backoff numbers to the B2 movements (section 5.6).
AC-5 (SNMP status exposure distinguished from SNMP-trap-out and device polling): SATISFIED -- section 7.1 gives both distinctions explicitly, each with its own sub-bullet and a named reason.
AC-6 (feature-contribution contract states concretely how a CAP-RELEASED capability's screen/job-type/alarm-source registration works, referencing C4 and C2 by name): SATISFIED -- section 4.2/4.3/4.4 name C4 section 2.2/2.5 and C2 section 2.1 by section number for each of the three registrations.
AC-7 (at least eight testable acceptance criteria for the B1/B2 movements this catalogue feeds): SATISFIED -- section 8 gives 11, tagged by movement (B1-9/B2-1/B2-3/B2-5b).
AC-8 (contradictions/open items section lists every document checked, states none found or names them precisely, no PO-reserved decision reopened): SATISFIED -- section 9 lists 13 documents checked by name/status, states 'none found' for contradictions with an explicit rationale for the two closest calls (the six-root baseline scope note; CAPABILITY_STATE_VOCABULARY_AND_PRESENTATION.md checked and explicitly not engaged), and names three genuinely open items for the PO.

Validation: full one-shot regression, foreground, awaited, against the final merged base (python -m pytest -q -n auto --dist worksteal, 183.81s): 3226 passed, 27 skipped, 2 failed -- the same pre-existing/unrelated DLP-token collisions (tests/test_dev_0_5b_auth_consumer_canonical_config.py, relay/NXS-LOCAL-0030-credential-profiles-reference-model.json) CURRENT_STATE.md's own baseline already documents, confirmed unchanged by this diff. git diff --check clean.
